tests.title: CRM login page loads with sign-in controls
tests.goal: The staging CRM exposes its sign-in form when a user opens the root URL.

steps.text: Open the staging CRM root URL.
Review the sign-in form controls.

expected.text: The browser reaches `/auth/login` without an HTTP error.
The page shows the heading "Log in to your store" and company, username/email, password, and LOGIN controls.

checks.label: The browser reaches `/auth/login` without an HTTP error.
The page shows the heading "Log in to your store" and company, username/email, password, and LOGIN controls.

notes: Login page at /auth/login with company, username/email, password and LOGIN.

tests.title: Store admin signs in to Storeberry Flower CRM
tests.goal: The dedicated store admin can authenticate and reach the CRM workspace.
data: Company, username, and password from SCRM_COMPANY, SCRM_USERNAME, and SCRM_PASSWORD in local .env.

steps.text: Open the staging CRM sign-in page.
Enter the dedicated Storeberry Flower company name, username, and password.
Select LOGIN.
Confirm that the CRM workspace opens.

expected.text: The browser leaves the /auth/login route and reaches the CRM Get Started workspace.
The CRM navigation shows the Get Started link.

checks.label: The browser leaves the /auth/login route and reaches the CRM Get Started workspace.
The CRM navigation shows the Get Started link.

notes: Shared account reached /get-start; wrong password shows "Password incorrect, 3 attempts remaining."

tests.title: CRM customer list loads with search controls
tests.goal: A CRM user can open the customer list and search without exposing customer data in test reports.

steps.text: Sign in to the CRM as the staging store admin.
Open Customers > Customers.
Confirm the customer count and both search controls are available.
Search for a unique value that should not match any member.

expected.text: The customer list loads and displays a numeric total.
A search field is available for Member ID, Name, Mobile, or Email, and a separate search field is available for Remark.
The unique no-match search returns `No. of Customer: 0`.

checks.label: The customer list loads and displays a numeric total.
A search field is available for Member ID, Name, Mobile, or Email, and a separate search field is available for Remark.
The unique no-match search returns `No. of Customer: 0`.

notes: List total 321; both search fields present; QA email search after delete returned No. of Customer: 0.

tests.title: Add Customer requires First Name and Email
tests.goal: The Add Customer form blocks submission when required identity fields are missing.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Customers > Add Customer.
Leave First Name and Email blank.
Select Save.

expected.text: The form stays open and indicates that First Name and Email are required.
No customer record is created and the customer count does not increase.

checks.label: The form stays open and indicates that First Name and Email are required.
No customer record is created and the customer count does not increase.

notes: Empty Save shows "The First Name is required. The Language Perference is required." Email is not flagged until First Name is filled (validation comes in stages). No customer created.

tests.title: Create customer respects email opt-in and member level
tests.goal: A CRM user can create a staging customer with an explicit opt-in choice and member level.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.
data: Member level selected from the available levels.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Customers > Add Customer.
Enter a unique QA first name and a non-routable example.invalid email address.
Set Opt-in to No and select a member level.
Save the record and reopen it from the customer directory.

expected.text: The new QA customer appears once in the directory.
Opt-in remains No and the selected member level is retained after reopening.
No email or marketing message is sent.

checks.label: The new QA customer appears once in the directory.
Opt-in remains No and the selected member level is retained after reopening.
No email or marketing message is sent.

notes: QA customer MEMy001164524 created with Opt-in No and Level 1; values kept after reopening; @example.com email.

tests.title: Reject duplicate customer email or Member ID values
tests.goal: Customer creation prevents a duplicate email or editable Member ID from creating a second record.
preconditions: At least one dedicated QA customer exists; Member ID branch requires that the CRM UI permits setting a Member ID.
data: Existing QA customer email and, if editable, Member ID selected dynamically.
Second customer uses a unique QA first name and example.invalid email for the untested identifier.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Add Customer.
Attempt to save a second QA customer with the existing QA customer email.
Verify the duplicate is rejected and no second record is created.
If Member ID can be set in the form, repeat with the existing QA Member ID and a unique email.

expected.text: Duplicate email is rejected with a visible validation message and no duplicate customer appears.
If Member ID is editable, duplicate Member ID is likewise rejected without creating a record.

checks.label: Duplicate email is rejected with a visible validation message and no duplicate customer appears.
If Member ID is editable, duplicate Member ID is likewise rejected without creating a record.

notes: Duplicate (uppercase) email rejected: "The email is already registered."

tests.title: Product form rejects a non-positive price
tests.goal: The product form rejects a zero or negative price without saving the product.
preconditions: A staging product form and an existing category are available.
data: Price: 0, then -1 only if the form allows a second validation attempt.
An existing category selected from the UI.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Add Product.
Enter a unique QA name, select an existing category, and enter price 0.
Attempt to save; if the form accepts the input, correct it and try -1.
Search product lists for the QA name.

expected.text: The form displays a price validation error for each attempted non-positive value.
No product is created with the invalid price.

checks.label: The form displays a price validation error for each attempted non-positive value.
No product is created with the invalid price.

notes: Negative input resets to 0; HKD 0.00 hidden product saved without message (id 3199, terminated after). Open question whether HKD 0 must be allowed; triage after product owner answers.

tests.title: Customer birthday rejects an impossible date
tests.goal: An impossible MM-DD birthday is never saved on a customer.
preconditions: A QA customer created for this test (email @example.com, opt-in No)

steps.text: Open the QA customer > Edit
Type 02-30 in Birthday (MM-DD), close the picker and Save
Reopen Edit and read Birthday
Repeat with 13-45, then with 05-15

expected.text: 02-30 and 13-45 are rejected with a validation message, or the previous birthday is kept
Birthday never becomes today's date unless typed
05-15 saves and shows 05-15 after reopening

checks.label: 02-30 and 13-45 are rejected with a validation message, or the previous birthday is kept
Birthday never becomes today's date unless typed
05-15 saves and shows 05-15 after reopening

notes: 02-30 and 13-45 saved as 10-27 (today); 05-15 saved correctly.

expected.text: Confirmation reads "Are you sure want to delete selected customers?"

checks.label: Confirmation reads "Are you sure want to delete selected customers?"
After OK the search shows No. of Customer: 0
Total count drops by exactly 1
Opening the old detail URL redirects to the customer list

notes: Only the QA row ticked; confirmation "Are you sure want to delete selected customers?"; search returns 0; detail URL redirects to list.
